chapterTitle: Chapter 7: Fundamental Principles of Organic Chemistry & Stereochemistry
title: Chapter 7: Fundamental Principles of Organic Chemistry & Stereochemistry
subject: chemistry-12

questions.question: Friedrich Wöhler synthesized urea in 1828 by evaporating an aqueous solution of which inorganic compound, disproving the Vital Force Theory?
questions.explanation: NH₄CNO (ammonium cyanate) rearranges upon heating to form H₂N-CO-NH₂ (urea), the first organic molecule prepared from an inorganic precursor.

questions.question: What is the hybridization and bond angle around the carbon atoms in ethene (H₂C=CH₂)?
questions.explanation: Each double-bonded carbon is bonded to three atoms (2 H, 1 C) with no lone pairs, using three sp² hybrid orbitals in a planar 120° arrangement.

questions.question: Which of the following heterocyclic compounds contains a five-membered ring containing a sulfur heteroatom?
questions.explanation: Thiophene (C₄H₄S) is a 5-membered aromatic heterocycle containing one sulfur atom. Furan contains oxygen, pyrrole contains nitrogen.

questions.question: Compounds having the same molecular formula but differing in the position of functional groups along the carbon chain are termed:
questions.explanation: Position isomers (e.g., 1-propanol vs 2-propanol; 1-butene vs 2-butene) have the same carbon skeleton and functional group at different positions.

questions.question: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) and Dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃) are classic examples of which type of isomerism?
questions.explanation: Both share the formula C₂H₆O, but ethanol has an alcohol (-OH) group while dimethyl ether contains an ether (-O-) linkage.

questions.question: Metamerism is exhibited by compounds belonging to the same homologous family having unequal distribution of alkyl groups on either side of a polyvalent functional group, such as:

options.B: Ethers (e.g., diethyl ether vs methyl propyl ether)

questions.explanation: C₂H₅-O-C₂H₅ (diethyl ether) and CH₃-O-C₃H₇ (methyl propyl ether) have the same formula C₄H₁₀O but differ in alkyl chains flanking the oxygen.

questions.question: Keto-enol tautomerism involves the rapid equilibrium migration of:

options.B: A proton (hydrogen atom) between carbon and oxygen accompanied by a shift of a double bond

questions.explanation: CH₃-CO-CH₃ ⇌ CH₃-C(OH)=CH₂; a proton migrates between the α-carbon and the carbonyl oxygen with simultaneous double bond relocation.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules can exhibit geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: 2-Butene has restricted rotation about the C=C bond and each sp² carbon is attached to two different substituents (-H and -CH₃), allowing cis and trans forms.

questions.question: A carbon atom bonded to four entirely different atoms or groups of atoms is defined as a:
questions.explanation: An asymmetric carbon center possesses no symmetry elements and produces non-superimposable mirror images.

questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds contains a chiral carbon and exhibits optical activity?
questions.explanation: In lactic acid, the central carbon is attached to four distinct groups: -H, -OH, -CH₃, and -COOH, conferring chirality.

questions.question: Molecules that are non-superimposable mirror images of each other are called:
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are chiral stereoisomers that rotate plane-polarized light in equal magnitudes but opposite directions (dextro and levo).

questions.question: An equimolar mixture of dextrorotatory and levorotatory enantiomers is optically inactive due to:
questions.explanation: A racemic mixture (±) has net zero optical rotation because equal concentrations of + and - enantiomers cancel each other externally.

questions.question: Meso-tartaric acid contains two chiral carbon atoms yet is completely optically inactive because of:

options.B: Internal compensation due to an internal plane of symmetry

questions.explanation: Meso compounds have an internal mirror plane where the top half's optical rotation is cancelled internally by the bottom half.

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for (CH₃)₂CH-CH₂-CH(CH₃)₂?
questions.explanation: The longest continuous carbon chain has 5 carbons (pentane) with methyl substituents at carbons 2 and 4.

questions.question: Which of the following organic reaction intermediates is a planar, sp²-hybridized species bearing a positive charge and 6 valence electrons?
questions.explanation: Carbocations (R₃C⁺) are sp² hybridized with an empty unhybridized p-orbital, having trigonal planar geometry and 6 valence electrons.

questions.question: The relative order of thermodynamic stability of carbocations is:
questions.explanation: Tertiary carbocations are stabilized by 9 hyperconjugative α-hydrogens and the electron-donating +I inductive effect of three alkyl groups.

questions.question: Homolytic fission of a covalent C-C single bond generates:

options.B: Two neutral free radicals each carrying an unpaired electron
options.D: A carbocation and a hydride ion

questions.explanation: In homolytic cleavage (symmetrical breaking), each bonded atom retains one electron of the bonding pair: A:B → A• + B•.

questions.question: Which of the following functional groups has the highest nomenclature priority according to IUPAC rules?
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids (-COOH) have the highest priority among the common functional groups.

questions.question: What is the C-C-C bond angle in the cyclohexane ring in its most stable 'chair' conformation?
questions.explanation: The chair conformation of cyclohexane is completely free from angle strain and eclipsing torsional strain, adopting the ideal tetrahedral 109.5° angle.

questions.question: An electrophile is defined as a chemical species that is:

options.A: Electron-rich and donates an electron pair (Lewis base)
options.B: Electron-deficient and accepts an electron pair to form a new bond (Lewis acid)

questions.explanation: Electrophiles ('electron-lovers') seek electron density; they may be cations (H⁺, NO₂⁺, Br⁺) or neutral Lewis acids (BF₃, AlCl₃, SO₃).

questions.question: Which of the following is a nucleophile?
questions.explanation: Ammonia has an unshared lone pair of electrons on nitrogen available for donation to electron-deficient centers, functioning as a nucleophile.

questions.question: What is the total number of structural isomers possible for the alkane with molecular formula C₅H₁₂ (Pentane)?
questions.explanation: C₅H₁₂ has 3 structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

questions.question: Stereoisomers that are not mirror images of each other are called:
questions.explanation: Diastereomers have different spatial arrangements but are not mirror images (e.g., cis/trans isomers, non-mirror pairs of stereoisomers with multiple chiral centers).

questions.question: Which of the following effects is a permanent electron-displacement effect transmitted through sigma bonds along a carbon chain due to electronegativity differences?
questions.explanation: The inductive effect is permanent and operates through σ-bonds, diminishing rapidly beyond three carbon-carbon bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following alkyl groups exhibits the strongest electron-donating (+I) inductive effect?
questions.explanation: The tertiary butyl group with three methyl groups has the largest electron-pushing inductive (+I) effect.

questions.question: What is the systematic IUPAC name for CH₂=CH-CH₂-C≡CH?
questions.explanation: When double and triple bonds are equidistant from ends, the double bond receives the lower locant: Pent-1-en-4-yne.

questions.question: The phenomenon of rotation of the plane of polarized light by a chiral substance is measured using an instrument called a:
questions.explanation: A polarimeter measures the angle of optical rotation (α) of plane-polarized light passing through a sample tube.

questions.question: Which of the following hybridized orbitals has the greatest s-character (50%) and therefore the highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: sp hybridized carbon has 50% s-character, holding electrons closest to the nucleus, making sp carbon the most electronegative.

questions.question: The conversion of an alkane to a branched isomer at 300°C in the presence of AlCl₃/HCl catalyst is known as:
questions.explanation: Straight-chain alkanes convert into branched isomers (e.g., n-butane to isobutane) via catalytic isomerization to boost octane numbers.

questions.question: How many sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds are present in one molecule of Ethyne (Acetylene, H-C≡C-H)?
questions.explanation: Two C-H single bonds (2 σ) and one C≡C triple bond (1 σ + 2 π) give a total of 3 σ and 2 π bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about enantiomers is FALSE?

options.A: They have identical boiling points and melting points
options.B: They have identical refractive indices and densities
options.C: They rotate plane-polarized light in identical directions
options.D: They interact differently with chiral biological receptors

questions.explanation: Enantiomers rotate plane-polarized light in OPPOSITE directions (+ and -) by equal magnitudes.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC suffix used for naming an ester?
questions.explanation: Esters are named as alkyl alkanoates (suffix -oate, e.g., ethyl ethanoate).

questions.question: Which of the following compounds exhibits functional group isomerism with propanoic acid (CH₃CH₂COOH)?
questions.explanation: Both share the formula C₃H₆O₂; propanoic acid is a carboxylic acid while methyl ethanoate is an ester.

questions.question: Free radicals are neutral species possessing an unpaired electron. Their geometry is generally:

options.A: Planar or shallow pyramidal undergoing rapid inversion

questions.explanation: Alkyl free radicals (R₃C•) are sp² hybridized planar species with the odd electron in an unhybridized 2p orbital.

questions.question: The specific rotation [α] of an optically active compound is expressed by the formula [α] = α / (l · c), where the path length (l) and concentration (c) are in units of:
questions.explanation: By definition, path length l is in decimeters (1 dm = 10 cm) and concentration c is in g/mL (or g/cm³).
